info.name: Music Band App
info.description:
# Music Band App -- API Collection

Manual test collection for every endpoint in the Spring Boot backend. Built for clicking
through in Postman, not for a developer audience -- read this description once before you
start.

## How auth works here (read this first)

This API does **not** use Bearer tokens. It uses two cookies plus a CSRF header:

1. **CSRF (double-submit cookie).** `GET /api/auth/csrf` makes the server set an
   `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie that JavaScript (and Postman) CAN read. Every state-changing request
   (POST/PUT/DELETE) must echo that cookie's value back as an `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header, or the
   server rejects it with 403 before your request even reaches application code. You do not
   have to do this by hand: this collection's **collection-level pre-request script**
   automatically reads the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie from Postman's cookie jar and injects the
   `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header on every mutating request for you. You only need to have run
   "Auth > Get CSRF Token" at least once in the current session.
2. **Session (JWT-in-httpOnly-cookie).** `POST /api/auth/login` sets an `ACCESS_TOKEN`
   cookie carrying the actual JWT, marked `httpOnly` (JavaScript can never read it) and
   `Secure` (HTTPS only, unless the backend explicitly disables that for local HTTP dev --
   see the environment file's notes). Postman's cookie jar stores and automatically resends
   httpOnly cookies on later requests to the same host, exactly like a real browser -- you
   will simply never see its value anywhere in Postman's UI, by design. That is not a bug in
   this collection.
3. **Logout** invalidates the session server-side by bumping the account's `tokenVersion`,
   not just by deleting the cookie -- any JWT issued before logout stops working immediately.

## Recommended run order

1. **Auth** folder, in order: "Get CSRF Token" then "Login". Do this first, every session.
2. **Public Site** and **Contact** need no login at all -- try these any time.
3. **Admin: Users / Audit / Groups / Sheet Music / Events / Public Content** all need an
   ADMIN account, logged in, AND the specific permission toggle for that feature area (see
   each folder's own description) -- see "First-time setup" below, this is not automatic.

## First-time setup (READ THIS -- there is no signup, and no seed data)

This backend has **no public signup and no `data.sql`/seed mechanism** (confirmed by reading
the actual source: no seed file exists anywhere in the repo, and the README documents no
bootstrap admin). You must create your first ADMIN account directly in Postgres:

```sql
-- Password hash below is a BCrypt hash (Spring's BCryptPasswordEncoder, the default cost
-- factor 10) of the plaintext password "ChangeMe123!" -- generate your own with e.g.
-- `python3 -c "import bcrypt; print(bcrypt.hashpw(b'ChangeMe123!', bcrypt.gensalt()).decode())"`
-- (pip install bcrypt first) if you want a different password. Match whatever you put here
-- to the adminPassword value in the environment file.
INSERT INTO user_account
    (email, password_hash, role, status, token_version, minor, consent_on_file,
     created_at, updated_at, version)
VALUES
    ('admin@example.com',
     '$2a$10$REPLACE_WITH_A_REAL_BCRYPT_HASH',
     'ADMIN', 'ACTIVE', 0, false, true, now(), now(), 0);
```

**Second, and easy to miss:** holding the `ADMIN` role is never enough on its own. Every
admin-panel write additionally requires a specific `Permission` toggle
(`MANAGE_USERS`, `MANAGE_ADMIN_ROLES`, `MANAGE_GROUPS`, `MANAGE_SHEET_MUSIC`,
`MANAGE_EVENTS`, `MANAGE_CONTENT`), checked in the service layer independently of the role.
As of this backend version **there is no HTTP endpoint that grants these** (confirmed by
reading `PermissionService` directly -- `grant()`/`revoke()` are plain Java methods with "no
controller exists yet" in their own Javadoc). Grant yourself every toggle by hand too:

```sql
INSERT INTO admin_permission (admin_id, permission)
SELECT id, unnest(ARRAY['MANAGE_USERS','MANAGE_ADMIN_ROLES','MANAGE_GROUPS',
                         'MANAGE_SHEET_MUSIC','MANAGE_EVENTS','MANAGE_CONTENT'])
FROM user_account WHERE email = 'admin@example.com';
```

Without this second step, logging in will succeed but almost every admin request in this
collection will fail with 403 Forbidden -- that is expected given the current state of the
API, not a bug in this collection.

## Everything else

- Folders below are ordered roughly public -> privileged: Auth, Public Site, Contact, then
  the ADMIN-only feature folders.
- "Create" requests that other requests depend on (Create Group, Create User, Create Event,
  etc.) have a **test script** that automatically saves the new id into a collection
  variable (e.g. `{{groupId}}`) so later requests in the same folder work without you
  copy-pasting anything, as long as you run requests top-to-bottom.
- Multipart upload requests (sheet music, album photos) need you to manually pick a real
  file in Postman's body editor -- that part cannot be pre-filled in a shared JSON file.

exec: // Auto-inject the CSRF header for every state-changing request.
// This API uses Spring Security's double-submit cookie CSRF pattern: the
// XSRF-TOKEN cookie (set by GET /api/auth/csrf, and refreshed by the server on
// every response after that) must be echoed back as the X-XSRF-TOKEN header on
// every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, or the server rejects the request with 403 before
// it reaches application code. Doing this by hand for every request would be the
// single most annoying part of testing this API manually, so it's automated here
// once, at the collection level, instead of duplicated into every request.
'[music-band-app] No XSRF-TOKEN cookie found yet. Run "Auth > 1. Get CSRF Token" ' +
'at least once in this session before sending mutating requests.'

variable.description: No HTTP endpoint issues these today -- must be obtained manually from the password_token table for testing.

item.name: Auth
item.description: CSRF bootstrap + login/activate/reset/logout. Run 'Get CSRF Token' then 'Login' first, every session -- almost nothing else in this collection works without both.

request.description: Run this FIRST, before anything else in this collection. It has no body and returns 204 No Content -- its only real job is to make the server set a fresh XSRF-TOKEN cookie in Postman's cookie jar. The collection's pre-request script (see the collection-level 'Pre-request Script' tab) reads that cookie and automatically adds it as the X-XSRF-TOKEN header on every POST/PUT/DELETE request from here on, so you never have to copy it manually.

Logs in and sets the httpOnly ACCESS_TOKEN cookie (the JWT). You will NOT see this cookie's value anywhere in Postman's UI -- httpOnly cookies are invisible to scripts and the cookie inspector shows them without a value/flag readout in some Postman versions, but Postman's cookie jar still stores and automatically resends it on every subsequent request to the same host, exactly like a real browser would. That is expected and correct; it does not mean login failed. Requires the XSRF-TOKEN cookie to already exist -- run 'Get CSRF Token' first.

exec: pm.test('Response has email and role', function () {

request.description: Sets the initial password for an account created via 'Admin: Users > Create User'. The one-time activationToken is only ever returned in that create response and is auto-saved into the {{activationToken}} / {{musicianActivationToken}} collection variables by that request's test script -- copy whichever one you need into the 'token' field below (or point it at {{activationToken}}) before sending. Does not require being logged in, but does require a fresh CSRF cookie/header.

IMPORTANT: as of this backend version there is NO self-service 'request a password reset' HTTP endpoint (checked AuthController/AuthService directly -- only activate() and resetPassword() exist, the latter has no public trigger). A RESET-type password_token row currently has no way to be created except directly in the database. This request is included for completeness / future use and works fine once you have a valid raw reset token (e.g. inserted by hand into the password_token table for manual testing), but there is nothing in the product today that emails one to a user. Set {{resetToken}} manually before using this.

Invalidates the current session server-side by bumping the account's tokenVersion (every JWT issued before this call becomes rejected, not just the cookie cleared client-side) and clears the ACCESS_TOKEN cookie. Requires being logged in (relies on the ACCESS_TOKEN cookie Postman is already holding).

item.name: Public Site
item.description: Unauthenticated reads: news, gallery, videos, courses, public events. No login, no CSRF token needed (GET requests only). Safe to run any time, in any order.

request.description: Public, unauthenticated. Published news posts.
Public, unauthenticated. Photos grouped by album, per the spec's 'album view' requirement.

Public, unauthenticated. Returns the raw image bytes (inline, cacheable) for a photo uploaded via 'Admin: Public Content > Upload Album Photo'. Set {{photoId}} to a real photo id first (that request does not currently auto-capture one -- check the response body of the upload request).
Public, unauthenticated.
Public, unauthenticated.
Public, unauthenticated concert/event listing -- deliberately a different surface from the internal calendar in 'Admin: Events'. Only shows events created with isPublic=true.

item.name: Contact
item.description: The one unauthenticated WRITE in the API. Still needs a CSRF cookie/header, so run 'Auth > Get CSRF Token' at least once first.

request.description: Public, unauthenticated -- the first unauthenticated WRITE in the API. Still requires a CSRF cookie/header exactly like the /api/auth POSTs, so run 'Auth > Get CSRF Token' at least once in this session first. On success, every ACTIVE admin gets an email notification (requires MAIL_HOST/MAIL_PORT/MAIL_FROM to be configured and reachable on the backend).

item.name: Admin: Users
item.description: Requires an ADMIN account, logged in, holding the MANAGE_USERS permission toggle (see collection description's 'First-time setup' for how to grant it -- there is no HTTP endpoint for it). Changing a user's role additionally requires MANAGE_ADMIN_ROLES.

request.description: Requires MANAGE_USERS (ordinary profile CRUD) -- but since this example sets role=ADMIN, it ALSO requires MANAGE_ADMIN_ROLES on the actor, per Permission.MANAGE_ADMIN_ROLES's own Javadoc ('any actor changing a target's role ... MUST additionally hold this permission'). The response includes a one-time activationToken -- captured below into {{activationToken}} -- hand it to 'Auth > Activate Account' to set that user's first password.

Requires MANAGE_USERS. role=MUSICIAN does NOT require MANAGE_ADMIN_ROLES. The created id is saved into {{musicianId}} so 'Admin: Groups > Assign Musician to Group' and the sheet-music/event scoping fields have something real to point at.
Requires MANAGE_USERS.
Requires MANAGE_USERS.
Requires MANAGE_USERS (and MANAGE_ADMIN_ROLES too if role is being changed).

Requires MANAGE_USERS. Blocks future logins and bumps tokenVersion (any existing session for that user is invalidated immediately). Cannot target yourself -- returns 403 SelfTargetNotAllowedException if {{userId}} equals the logged-in actor's own id.

item.name: Admin: Audit
item.description: Requires an ADMIN account, logged in (base role gate only -- no additional permission toggle exists for audit specifically, per SecurityConfig's own comment). Read-only history; there is no write endpoint here by design.

request.description: Read-only history for one entity, addressed by (entityType, entityId). No create endpoint exists -- rows are written internally whenever another admin action happens (e.g. GROUP_CREATED). {{auditEntityType}} defaults to 'Group' so this works out of the box after you run 'Admin: Groups > Create Group' -- other real entityType values seen in the codebase: UserAccount, Collection, SheetMusic, Event. Swap the path variables to inspect any of those instead.

item.name: Admin: Groups
item.description: Requires an ADMIN account, logged in, holding the MANAGE_GROUPS permission toggle.

request.description: Requires MANAGE_GROUPS.
Requires MANAGE_GROUPS.
Requires MANAGE_GROUPS.
Requires MANAGE_GROUPS.
Requires MANAGE_GROUPS. Returns the minimal {id, email, role} shape, deliberately not the richer user DTO, to avoid leaking MANAGE_USERS-domain PII to a MANAGE_GROUPS-only actor.
Requires MANAGE_GROUPS. Run 'Admin: Users > Create User (Musician example)' first so {{musicianId}} is populated.
Requires MANAGE_GROUPS. Run this before 'Delete Group' if you assigned a musician above.

Requires MANAGE_GROUPS. Returns 409 Conflict (GroupInUseException) if the group still has members -- run 'Unassign Musician from Group' for every member first. Placed last in this folder deliberately.

item.name: Admin: Sheet Music
item.description: Collections require ADMIN + MANAGE_SHEET_MUSIC. Uploading a piece requires just MANAGE_SHEET_MUSIC (any authenticated role can reach this path, but the service layer still gates the mutation). Downloading only requires being authenticated AND in scope for that specific piece -- try downloading as a musician who isn't scoped to see the IDOR-safe 404 behavior.

request.description: Requires MANAGE_SHEET_MUSIC. A collection is a folder sheet music pieces are filed under.

Requires being authenticated (any role) -- MANAGE_SHEET_MUSIC is additionally required to actually upload. Multipart form: select a real file for the 'file' field in Postman's body editor before sending (Postman cannot embed a file for you in a shared JSON collection). allScope=true here means every authenticated user can download it; leave groupIds/musicianIds disabled unless you want to scope access instead.

IDOR-safe: returns 404 (never 403) whether the id does not exist or you simply cannot access it, so this also doubles as an access-control test -- try it while logged in as a musician who is not in scope for the piece.

item.name: Admin: Events
item.description: The internal calendar. Listing/viewing only requires being authenticated (any role) and in scope for that event; creating/editing/cancelling additionally requires MANAGE_EVENTS.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Spring Concert",
  "description": "Annual spring concert at the village hall",
  "location": "Village Hall",
  "startsAt": "2026-05-15T18:00:00Z",
  "isPublic": true,
  "allScope": true,
  "groupIds": [],
  "musicianIds": []
}

request.description: Requires being authenticated (any role); MANAGE_EVENTS is additionally required to create/edit/cancel. startsAt must be an ISO-8601 instant (UTC). isPublic=true also makes it show up in 'Public Site > Get Public Events'.
Requires being authenticated. Scoped: only events the logged-in actor can access are returned (cancelled ones included, with status shown).
IDOR-safe: 404 whether it doesn't exist or you can't access it.

request.description: Requires MANAGE_EVENTS. Note: access scope (groupIds/musicianIds) can only be set at creation, not edited here.
Requires MANAGE_EVENTS. Non-destructive, idempotent lifecycle end-state -- there is deliberately no delete endpoint for events.

item.name: Admin: Public Content Management
item.description: Requires an ADMIN account, logged in, holding the MANAGE_CONTENT permission toggle. These are the write-side counterparts of the read-only 'Public Site' folder -- create something here, then re-run the matching Public Site request to see it appear.

request.description: Requires MANAGE_CONTENT. Shows up immediately in 'Public Site > Get News'.
Requires MANAGE_CONTENT. Create an album first, then upload photos into it below.

Requires MANAGE_CONTENT. Multipart form, mirrors the sheet-music upload shape: select a real image file for the 'file' field before sending. The resulting photo id is saved to {{photoId}} and is what 'Public Site > Get Gallery Photo File' downloads.
Requires MANAGE_CONTENT. Shows up immediately in 'Public Site > Get Videos'.
